title: Unnecessary Thread-Safe Wrapping (The Over-Guarded Field)
pattern: Wrapping types in thread-safe containers (`Arc<Mutex<T>>`) when they are only ever accessed or mutated from a single thread.
why_bad: Forces costly mutex locking operations, atomic count increments, and potential deadlocks on single-threaded data.
detection: A mutex-wrapped type whose lock methods are only invoked within a single thread context.
counterexample: Genuinely shared data accessed concurrently across distinct threads.
fix: Remove `Arc<Mutex<T>>` wrapping and use standard raw access (or `Rc<RefCell<T>>` if local interior mutability is required).
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust For Rustaceans* (2021); Herlihy, Maurice, *The Art of Multiprocessor Programming*.
